newsitem.title: USA: Farm Fresh debt falls three points, CEO departs.
newsitem.headline: Farm Fresh debt falls three points, CEO departs.

text.p: Farm Fresh Inc debt fell three points in secondary trading following the resignation of its Chief Executive Officer and an ensuing downgrade to the company's senior notes, traders said.
Debt of Farm Fresh, a unit of FF Holdings, fell three points and was quoted at 82-1/2 bid, 83-1/2 offer, after the news, traders said.

Moody's Investors Service cut the company's senior notes to Caa from B3 on Tuesday after the Virginia-based supermarket chain announced late Monday that its CEO, Michael Julian, resigned his position as an officer of the company.

Moody's said the resignation, and the absence of any evidence that Farm Fresh is moving forward with a restructuring plan to preserve the position of its senior note holders, prompted the rating action.
"Its been widely speculated that the company would need to restructure at some point," said Sharon Meyers Levine, an analyst with NationsBank Corp.
"The credit agency seems convinced that they don't see any imminent signs of a restructuring and view his (CEO) leaving as negative," Levine said.
The ratings, which were lowered last year were kept under review as Moody's cited concerns over the company's restructuring plan, high leverage, and the parent's weak capital structure.

"We had lowered the ratings in September, keeping them on review for possible further downgrade...as there's large cash pay interest which limits their defensive ability as competitors move into the market," said Mike Rowan, senior analyst at Moody's Investors Service.
Moody's said interest on the parent company debt converts to cash pay in April of 1998.

"Although the supermarket does have a material hold ond solid market share in the Virgina Beach-Hampton Roads market new competitors are moving in and they need to be able to access capital to stay competitive," Rowan said.

Moody's said it is likely that the principal amount of the senior notes may be compromised in a restructuring. Its opinion is based on the magnitude of the company's leverage relative to a "realistic" enterprise value and the subordination of the senior notes to secured bank debt.
Secured bank debt totaled $17 million in September.
Farm Fresh hired Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette late last year to help the company with its restructruring plan, analysts said.
